simple.meaning: חֲבַל (chăbal) is a Hebrew word meaning “harm (personal or pecuniary).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חֲבַל (H2257) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 4:22, with occurrences in Ezra, Daniel.

definitions.full: H2257. chabal חֲבָל noun masculine 6:24 hurt, injury ; — absolute ׳ח Dan 3:25 ; 6:24 , compare RÉS 362A 2 ; emphatic חֲבָלָא Ezra 4:22 .

occurrences.englishText: Be careful that you not be slack doing so. Why should damage grow to the hurt of the kings?
He answered, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”

The king commanded, and they brought those men who had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions mauled them, and broke all their bones in pieces, before they came to the bottom of the den.
